text: Huh, that doesn't tickle at all. Why not?
Turns out, even an ancient Greek philosopher wondered about this - or so the story goes.
Tickling only happens when you have no idea when or where that touch is coming.
But when it's your own hand, your brain already knows exactly when and where it's about to land.
So by the time it touches you, there's nothing left to be surprised about.
But add a tiny delay - say, with a robot arm - and even your own hand can tickle you again.
Break the prediction, even slightly, and the tickle comes right back.
